reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the claimed CO oxidation activity advantage and hydrothermal stability of Pd1@HEFO over Pd@CeO2, but does not provide data on the specific synthesis method, lattice-oxygen reducibility mechanism, or long-term cyclic durability (>10,000 cycles) proposed in the hypothesis.
premises: Pd1@HEFO shows dramatically lower CO oxidation onset temperature (~80 °C) than Pd@CeO2 (223 °C) under the tested conditions.
Atomically dispersed Pd in Pd1@HEFO remains stable without agglomeration or sintering after hydrothermal treatment.
The high-entropy fluorite oxide support enhances lattice-oxygen reducibility and oxygen activation compared to CeO2.
Strong metal-support interactions in Pd1@HEFO suppress Pd sintering and deactivation.
The synthesis method (mechanical milling + 900 °C calcination) yields atomically dispersed Pd anchored in the HEFO lattice.
